source.title: Anaphase-promoting complex/cyclosome protein Cdc27 is a target for curcumin-induced cell cycle arrest and apoptosis.
source.status_limit: No correction/retraction/version relation present in this saved Europe PMC result; not a complete integrity assessment.

identity.preparation: Laboratory curcumin reagent; no delivery formulation specified. Not Gemini-Cur, turmeric extract or an oral supplement.
missing: Measured cell-medium concentration or free fraction

separate_control.name: Dehydrozingerone
separate_control.role: Actually administered structural comparator in Figure 3B/C; not an untested target-derived name.

overlap_check.existing_curcumin_appraisal: new-gemini-cur concerns mPEG urethane gemini surfactant nanoparticles in HCT116, DOI10.3390/molecules27113470; not this reagent or study.
overlap_check.separate_oocyte_context: oocyte-metabolism-qualification.md reports curcumin with no apparent GVBD/polar-body effect in another source; no new primary reading of that experiment here.

models.main: DAOY medulloblastoma cells, cultured in MEM with 10% FBS, glutamine and penicillin/streptomycin; source states all lines obtained from ATCC.
models.normal_cell_limit: MDCK is an established canine kidney-derived epithelial line, not primary normal human tissue. Official ATCC MDCK identity supports lineage only; the paper gives no exact catalog/subclone authentication. HT1376 is a relatively resistant bladder-cancer comparator, not a normal cell.
models.unexplained_native_label: Figure 4B contains an HBEC blot block not listed in the caption A panel and not defined in the Methods. It is not part of Figure 4C/D six-line cytotoxicity/apoptosis comparison; no normal-human safety or functional benefit is assigned.
models.animals: Supplementary Figure S1 compares Cdc27 protein in corn-oil-control versus curcumin-treated Smo/Smo medulloblastoma tumor specimens from prior work. Three labeled lanes per arm; independent animal n is not established by lane count.

experiments.model: DAOY, double-thymidine synchronization (2 mM for 18 h, release 9 h, 2 mM for 18 h)
experiments.exposure: Release with 0, 10 or 20 µM curcumin; 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20 h
experiments.control: No-curcumin release; only about 48% G0/G1 initially
experiments.outcome: Delayed cycle progression/reentry; no sub-G0/G1 fraction detected over this interval despite delay.
experiments.limit: Incomplete synchronization; no division-fidelity outcome. See Table S1 prose discrepancy.

experiments.model: DAOY, thymidine 2 mM for 24 h, release 3 h, nocodazole 100 nM for 12 h
experiments.exposure: After washout, DMSO or 10/20 µM curcumin for 0–10 h, sampled every 2 h
experiments.outcome: Delayed G2/M exit and increased sub-G0/G1. At 10 h, 20 µM G2/M 48.95 ± 10.95%; sub-G0/G1 11.67 ± 6.07% versus 5.52 ± 0.38% control.
experiments.limit: Reported 69.8% remaining is normalized to initial G2/M, not 69.8% of all cells; DNA content cannot separate G2 from M or identify the same cells.

experiments.model: DAOY unsynchronized, G1/S release and G1/S release 8 h before drug addition
experiments.outcome: Higher LDH release in cells exposed after the 8-hour release; authors describe about threefold higher cytotoxicity at 20 µM than the other schedules.
experiments.limit: This G2/M-scheduled LDH arm is not the thymidine/nocodazole protocol; no mitotic lineage tracking. Figure states three independent experiments, SEM.

experiments.exposure: Figure 2A: 0, 5, 10, 15, 20 µM for 12 h; 2B: 0, 5, 10, 20 µM; 2C: 0, 6, 12, 24 h (concentration not labeled in its caption/image)
experiments.control: Loading controls and other cell-cycle/APC proteins
experiments.outcome: Cdc27 higher-molecular-weight bands increase with concentration/time; APC2, p55Cdc20, cyclin A/E expression not noticeably changed in 2A; APC7/8 do not show analogous crosslinked bands.
experiments.limit: Long/short exposure panels are the same blot where stated; no molecular identification of a covalent linkage.

experiments.exposure: Curcumin covalently immobilized on epoxy-Sepharose; 500 µg lysate + 20 µl beads, 3 h at 4°C
experiments.control: Matched beads without curcumin; two curcumin-bead preparations; BubR1 nonspecific-binding control immunoblot
experiments.outcome: Cdc27 recovered, preferentially the higher/phosphorylated band.
experiments.limit: Lysate affinity capture, not purified-protein affinity, direct-contact or covalent-site measurement; complex co-capture not excluded. BubR1 was assayed as a binding control, not restored or functionally rescued.

experiments.exposure: 3B: curcumin 20 µM versus DHZ 40 µM for 3, 6, 9, 24 h; 3C: each compound 0, 5, 10, 20 µM for 16 h
experiments.control: DHZ structural comparator, no-drug control and GAPDH loading
experiments.outcome: Curcumin induces high-MW Cdc27 bands and dose-dependent LDH release; DHZ lacks the analogous band shift and has little LDH increase. Native graph at 20 µM is approximately 47% curcumin versus 9–10% DHZ cytotoxicity, compared with approximately 7–8% baseline.
experiments.limit: Graph values are visual approximations, not raw data. Three independent experiments/SEM for LDH. Neither general DHZ inactivity nor DHZ safety or MVA benefit follows.

experiments.model: Expression and six-line function panels as listed
experiments.exposure: 4C: 0, 5, 10, 20 µM for 24 h; 4B/D and S4: 20 µM at 0, 4, 8, 24 h; S3 cycle release: 0, 10, 20 µM up to 10 h
experiments.control: Low-phospho-Cdc27 MDCK/HT1376 compared with more responsive lines; phosphatase supports upper-band phosphorylation; loading controls
experiments.outcome: Differential LDH and PARP/caspase responses; DAOY and NT2 strongly responsive, MDCK/HT1376 much weaker. NT2 mitotic-exit delay contrasts with comparatively unchanged MDCK profiles. Acetylated-tubulin increase also tracks responsive lines.
experiments.limit: Correlation across lines is not Cdc27 phosphorylation necessity or a validated predictive biomarker. No normal-cell equivalence or safety claim, and no normal-cell functional rescue.

experiments.exposure: 0, 20, 40 µM curcumin following release; A 0.5–4 h, B 2/4 h
experiments.outcome: Cyclin B1/securin persist; APC2, p55Cdc20 and cyclin D1 do not show analogous changes.
experiments.limit: Substrate persistence supports altered APC/C function but is not selective target proof.

experiments.exposure: 0, 10, 20, 40 µM for 8 h; caption says double-thymidine arrest
experiments.outcome: Reduced Cdc27–p55Cdc20 association while APC2/APC8 association persists; Cdh1 not detected under these conditions.
experiments.limit: Results prose refers to G2/M release, whereas caption specifies double-thymidine preparation; preserve this preparation mismatch.

experiments.locator: Figure 5D / Methods in vitro APC assay
experiments.model: Lysate from treated DAOY cells, not purified APC/C
experiments.exposure: Mitotic release in DMSO or 20/40 µM curcumin for 1/2 h; assay adds UbcH10, ubiquitin, radiolabeled cyclin B1 N1–102, ATPγS and MG132
experiments.control: DMSO lysate, reaction time and ubiquitinated-substrate signal
experiments.outcome: Reduced cyclin-fragment ubiquitination in the 2-hour drug-treated lysates versus increasing control activity.
experiments.limit: No purified direct-inhibitor IC50, free-drug-carryover separation or Cdc27-resistant rescue. MG132 and 35S-methionine are assay reagents here.

experiments.model: Previously obtained Smo/Smo medulloblastoma tumor specimens
experiments.exposure: Curcumin versus corn-oil control; current paper does not restate dose, schedule or route
experiments.outcome: Authors report lower tumor Cdc27; high-MW crosslinked species not detected in vivo.
experiments.limit: Qualitative reused-specimen protein comparison, not a new tumor-growth/survival or PK experiment. Prior reported survival/DAOY-xenograft benefit is cited but not independently qualified here.

strongest_positive: Ordinary curcumin causes dose- and cell-cycle-dependent DAOY cytotoxicity, delayed mitotic exit and apoptosis-related changes, accompanied by Cdc27 affinity recovery/high-MW bands, reduced Cdc20 association and lower treated-lysate cyclin-fragment ubiquitination. These are real cell and biochemical results; exclusive Cdc27 causality is unproved.
important_nulls: No detected sub-G0/G1 in the double-thymidine release interval despite cycle delay
Weak response of MDCK and cancer line HT1376 under tested exposure
DHZ little LDH increase/no analogous high-MW Cdc27 band under specified assays
No in-vivo crosslinked Cdc27 species detected
Other APC-component association/expression controls relatively preserved as specified
Cdh1 not detected in the Figure 5C IP conditions
target_attribution: The data support a Cdc27/APC/C-associated mechanism; they do not establish purified direct binding, a mapped covalent Cdc27 site, selective Cdc27 inhibition, necessity/sufficiency or a clinically validated phospho-Cdc27 response biomarker.

BUB1B_relevance.measured: BubR1 immunoblot included in Figure 3A as nonspecific affinity-binding control.
not_measured: Leu737Ter/Asn1002Lys MVA cells or animal model
Chromosome segregation fidelity or aneuploidy rescue
Normal muscle output or other normal-tissue functional compensation
BUB1B_relevance.mechanistic_context: APC/C restraint is a concrete, testable timing hypothesis downstream of the spindle assembly checkpoint. This study demonstrates cell-cycle restraint and cancer-cell death, not restoration of checkpoint function, faithful division or healthy output.

animal_exposure_scope: Current study has reused mouse-tumor protein blots, no new animal efficacy regimen or measured exposure. Do not inherit prior 2011 efficacy paper as fully read. No inference that food, turmeric or oral curcumin supplements attain the 10–40 µM experimental concentrations.
relative_priority: Retain ordinary curcumin as a distinct cancer-cell/APC/C mechanism comparator and DHZ as a tested negative comparator. This source supplies neither BUB1B restoration nor normal functional compensation to displace provisional niacin/apitegromab or the conditional everolimus probe; those nominees also remain unproved for MVA. No measured MVA harm is inferred from tumor-cell killing.
source_issues: Table S2 prose percentages normalize to initial G2/M fraction rather than the full population.
Table S1 56.9% not-reentered wording is not reconciled with reported whole-culture phase percentages.
Figure 5C preparation differs between caption and surrounding Results wording.
HBEC appears only as an undefined extra Figure 4B blot block; not a six-line function-assay arm.
Current mouse blots reuse earlier specimens; lane count is not verified independent animal n.
bounded_followups: If quantitative animal efficacy, PK or regimen comparison is needed, independently qualify the cited 2011 paper DOI10.1186/1471-2407-11-144.
Resolving Cdc27 necessity, direct-contact chemistry or normal BUB1B-mutant functional effects requires experiments not reported here; these are gaps, not inferred benefits.

root_read_scope.source_precision: Only genuine S1 prose and S2 reference-denominator limits retained; no false row-sum claim.

integrated_appraisals.evidence_scope: Complete 2012 scientific main/captions, all five native main figures and six supplementary TIFFs (two tables/four figures); source-specific limitations retained.
integrated_appraisals.route: Ordinary curcumin / cancer-cell Cdc27–APC/C-associated arrest and apoptosis
integrated_appraisals.disposition: Retain experimental cancer-cell mechanism comparator; do not nominate as BUBR1 restoration or infer oral-supplement efficacy
integrated_appraisals.rationale: Laboratory curcumin at 10–40 µM delays DAOY cycle progression and, depending on schedule, increases cytotoxicity/apoptosis. Cdc27 affinity capture, high-MW bands, reduced Cdc20 association and lower treated-lysate cyclin-fragment ubiquitination support an APC/C-associated mechanism without purified direct binding, covalent-site or Cdc27-necessity proof. MDCK and HT1376 are less responsive under tested conditions, not broad normal-tissue safety evidence. BubR1 is an affinity-binding control, not restored. Reused mouse-tumor blots show lower Cdc27 but no detected crosslinked species; no new animal efficacy/PK or MVA function is established. Distinct from Gemini-Cur nanoparticles.

integrated_appraisals.evidence_scope: Complete 2012 scientific main/captions, all five native main figures and six supplementary TIFFs (two tables/four figures); source-specific limitations retained.
integrated_appraisals.route: Dehydrozingerone / tested structural comparator in curcumin–Cdc27 study
integrated_appraisals.disposition: Retain dose-bounded negative experimental comparator; no general inactivity, safety or MVA-rescue claim
integrated_appraisals.rationale: In DAOY cells, half-curcumin/dehydrozingerone at 40 µM for 3–24 h lacks the analogous high-MW Cdc27 bands seen with 20 µM curcumin. In the separate equal-concentration 16-hour LDH assay (0–20 µM each), DHZ has little cytotoxicity increase while curcumin rises substantially. These actual null/weak responses constrain this assay only; they do not establish DHZ efficacy, human exposure, normal-cell safety or BUB1B/MVA rescue.
